items.description: A developer under deadline pressure could add a convenience 'admin override' or 'update' path to the audit store that violates append-only guarantees.
items.mitigation: Enforce append-only at the schema/permission layer in addition to the application layer (e.g. database-level revoke of UPDATE/DELETE grants for the application's service account on the audit event table), not solely via application code review.

items.description: Maker-checker separation could be bypassed by an analyst holding two accounts or sharing credentials.
items.mitigation: Out of scope for this feature's technical controls (identity/account governance is owned by IAM), but flagged to Security as a process control dependency; the system enforces identity-level separation given the identities it is told about.

items.description: Sensitive data could leak into logs indirectly through unhandled exception stack traces that include exception objects carrying trade data.
items.mitigation: Exception handling middleware must serialize only a fixed error code and correlation id to logs, never the raw exception object's message or data properties when it originates from the resolution or export path.

items.description: The CI log-content scan (NFR-1 verification) could produce false negatives if new fields are added to telemetry payloads without updating the scan's allow-list check.
items.mitigation: Implement the scan as an allow-list (fail on any unrecognized field) rather than a deny-list (fail only on known-bad fields), so new fields must be explicitly allow-listed before they can ship.
